Leah (support): flagging a customer escalation from BlueFin — they report sudden p95/p99 spikes for short prompts starting ~2026-03-15T09:12Z. Median fine (~30-45ms) but p99 hitting 650-900ms sporadically. They think it correlated with last night's batcher config change. attaching their sample req id bf-9001 and request snippets.

Ajay (runtime): which config was changed? we pushed the continuous-batcher hold_window default bump to 10ms and enabled batch_coalesce=true last night for throughput.

Leah (support): correct — BlueFin is low-token workloads (5-20 tokens). their logs show some requests with dispatch_wait ~120ms then total latency shows 700ms. sample log: ``[2026-03-15T09:15:03Z] req=bf-9001 recv dispatch_wait=118ms batch_size=1 worker_wait=560ms total=688ms``

Maria (oncall): deploy-bot any deploys/config-rolls around 08:50-09:05Z? :eyes:

deploy-bot: continuous-batcher config roll: sha a7e9f3d rolled 2026-03-15T08:45:00Z by ajay; hold_window_ms: 10 -> previously 3ms.

Sam (sre): started an internal repro using BlueFin sample payloads against staging with bursty arrivals (microbursts). I see tail outliers too. Baseline run (post-roll) p95 ~92ms p99 ~740ms. Repro command (bash):

```
# simulate microbursts: 400 requests in bursts of 50 with tiny jitter
for round in {1..8}; do
  for i in {1..50}; do
    curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $STG" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
      -d '{"model":"redwood-small","input":"ok","max_tokens":6}' \
      https://staging-api.internal/v1/generate &
    sleep 0.002
  done
  wait
  sleep 0.25
done
```

Sam (sre): tracing the request path shows a pattern: the batcher holds for hold_window_ms (10ms), flushes, the selected worker then hits a kernel-selection / kv-cache-fill path that causes an additional blocking wait (~500-700ms) for some requests. If a request arrives at batcher right before worker becomes available, it may get flushed and then queued behind worker warmup -> large tail.

Ajay (runtime): thanks — this is the classic overlapping-waits problem: hold timer + worker warmup/backpressure. Increasing hold_window was meant to increase batch sizes but for short prompt workloads it increases the chance of late-arrival singles being flushed into slow worker states. We need a short-prompt policy.

Maria (oncall): mitigation options (quick to longer-term):
- quick: lower hold_window for short prompts or set hold_window=0 for single-request batches
- quick: immediate-dispatch threshold for batch_size==1 to avoid waiting logic entirely for singles
- mid: pre-warm a small pool of hot workers dedicated to sub-64-token workloads
- long: prompt-length-aware routing + backpressure-aware dispatch (avoid flushing into warmed workers)
Which do we want to try first?

Leah (support): BlueFin wants a quick fix now. They prefer config change rather than infra prep.

Ajay (runtime): I can push a hotfix config that scopes hold_window per prompt-length. Suggested override:

```
continuous_batcher:
  hold_window_ms:
    default: 10
    under_64_tokens: 2
  immediate_dispatch_for_single_request: true
  telemetry_label: "batcher.hold_override=short_prompt_hotfix"
```

Ajay (runtime): it's a single-file config change deployable as a staged canary. low risk and reversible.

Sam (sre): ran the same repro with the override applied to a 10% canary pool. Results: baseline p99 740ms -> canary p99 140ms; p95 improved slightly (92ms -> 86ms). CPU on canary nodes +6% due to more immediate dispatches. No errors observed. I added a gate to our CI smoke test: fail if p99_short_prompt > 300ms.

Leah (support): BlueFin validated against the canary nodes and reported tail dropped to ~150ms for them. they asked what changed. I explained we temporarily lowered the hold window for short prompts and enabled quicker single-request dispatch. They were satisfied.

Maria (oncall): plan: push to hosted 100% after 30m observation window if no regressions, then issue Dedicated advisory. Ajay, please add a telemetry flag so we can search historical events. Sam, keep the new CI assertion.

Ajay (runtime): done. rolling to 100% now as metrics stayed stable during the canary. PR: https://git.internal/redwood/continuous-batcher/pull/558 — includes config, rollout notes, and canary guardrails (p99_short_prompt < 300ms).

Sam (sre): notes for postmortem: our default tuning change targeted throughput but didn't consider prompt-length distribution. Action items: add an integration test that simulates short-prompt microbursts, add a prompt-length-based default to the runtime, and instrument worker-warmup metric to trigger dynamic hold_window reductions. I'll draft the postmortem doc.

Ajay (runtime): longer-term: consider hot-worker pools or faster kernel caching for small models. Also adding metric "batcher.flush_cause" to distinguish timer vs size vs override.

Maria (oncall): ops checklist completed: canary ok -> promoted; support notified; CI guard added; postmortem items assigned. Leah, please confirm BlueFin is happy and close the support ticket.

Leah (support): BlueFin confirmed full rollout fixed their issue. closing the ticket and marking escalation resolved. :white_check_mark: Thanks everyone.

Sam (sre): leaving this thread open for the postmortem doc link. Will update when ready.

(End of thread)
